newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia wages seen up, output growth down in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia wages seen up, output growth down in Q1.

text.p: Manufacturing wages in Malaysia are likely to spurt upward in the first quarter of 1997 while production volumes are expected to decline, the Malaysian Institute of Economic Research (MIER) said on Wednesday.
Its quarterly survey of 168 business organisations also found that exports would continue to sustain growth more than domestic demand.
Some 76 percent of the respondents in the survey expected no change or a decline in prices of their products, boding well for containing inflationary pressures, MIER said.
"The most prominent feature of the first quarter of 1997 will be a likely increase in manufacturing wages across the board," the survey report said.

Sixty-four percent of the firms surveyed expected wage costs to rise in the first three months of the year -- a 1.7-fold increase on a year-on-year basis and a rise of 39 percent over the previous quarter's expectations, it said.
"In the coming three months, wage increases will most likely prevail in the wood, paper, chemical, rubber, metal, electrical and machinery sectors," the report said.
Production volumes are expected to drop, with only 40 percent of the firms surveyed expecting output to rise.
"Lower production volumes will be most prevalent among non-metallic manufacturing firms," the report said.
Growth prospects for the manufacturing sector hinge more on exports than domestic demand, it said. Thirty-six percent of the firms expected exports to rise, unchanged on a yearly basis.
But 34 percent expected domestic sales to go up in the first quarter, compared with 47 percent in the same period last year.

Despite the surge in wage increase expectations, prices on the whole could decline in the first quarter, the survey said. Fifty-nine percent of the firms surveyed expected no price changes and 17 percent said they would decline.
Prices are expected to remain stable mostly in the food, textiles, wood, paper, rubber, plastics, metal and electrical sectors, the survey said.
